incidents.name: PHP-CGI argument injection on Windows
incidents.note: Only PHP run as CGI behind Apache on Windows, in certain code pages. Exploited in the wild within days; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: php-cgi and PHP-FPM remote code execution
incidents.note: Both in CISA KEV. CVE-2012-1823 needs PHP run as a CGI script (php-cgi): a query string without an equals sign is read as command-line options. CVE-2019-11043 needs PHP-FPM behind nginx with a common fastcgi_split_path_info setup; used in ransomware attacks per KEV.

incidents.name: Heartbleed
incidents.note: Reads server or client memory over TLS, including private keys. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: CMS AuthEnvelopedData stack overflow
incidents.note: Reachable without a key where the product parses untrusted CMS or PKCS#7 data (S/MIME, for example). Fixed in the January 2026 OpenSSL releases.

incidents.name: Java4Shell (HotSpot AVX-512 Base64 decoder heap overflow)
incidents.note: Only on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake and later Xeons and some Core chips, AMD Zen 4 and later); ARM64 is not affected. Also affected: Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack 8u511b33-perf (fixed in 8u513-perf) and GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20.0.3. Interim mitigations (either one): -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (preferred; VulnCheck tested it with -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions ahead of it), or -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only, since JVMs on ARM64 fail to start with it. Crashing an affected JVM is easy (a burst of malformed requests); code execution needs heap grooming and a separate exploit profile for each application, and no public exploit does that. A proof of concept that triggers the bug is public, VulnCheck supplies a full exploit to its customers, and probing and blind exploit attempts have been seen since 18 November (GreyNoise, watchTowr); no confirmed compromise and not in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-20.

incidents.name: Exploited flaws without version data (CISA KEV)
incidents.note: Each of these is in CISA KEV, but its CVE record has no usable version data, so no product is flagged by version for them.

incidents.name: NGINX2Root
incidents.note: CVE-2026-123007 (HTTP/2, unauthenticated) is the remote code execution entry point; the disclosure chains it with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root. Disabling HTTP/2 blocks only CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. A proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 is public (Rapid7); not in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-19.

incidents.name: Tomcat partial PUT remote code execution
JSP upload through HTTP PUT
incidents.note: Needs HTTP PUT enabled (readonly=false on the Default servlet). Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: EncryptInterceptor bypass
incidents.note: Affects clusters that rely on EncryptInterceptor, and only these three releases. In CISA KEV since August 2026.

incidents.name: May 2026 HTTP/2, DIGEST and security-constraint fixes
incidents.note: Scored critical by CVSS, though Apache rates them low to moderate. Exploits are public, and the fixes set off advisories from Atlassian, Ubuntu and others. Tomcat 8.5 is affected and gets no fix.

incidents.name: JMX listener and Windows PUT remote code execution
incidents.note: Both in CISA KEV. CVE-2016-8735 needs JmxRemoteLifecycleListener in use and the JMX ports reachable. CVE-2017-12615 is Tomcat 7 on Windows with HTTP PUT enabled (the readonly parameter set to false); used in ransomware attacks per KEV.

incidents.name: Jolokia MBean remote code execution
incidents.note: Needs a login to the web console's Jolokia API. In CISA KEV since April 2026.

incidents.name: Fileserver upload remote code execution
incidents.note: An HTTP PUT then MOVE to the Fileserver web application uploads and runs a file. In CISA KEV. The Fileserver was removed in 5.14.0.

incidents.name: Struts file upload path traversal (S2-066, S2-067)
OGNL and REST plugin remote code execution (S2-052, S2-057, S2-061)
incidents.note: All three are exploited in the wild and in CISA KEV. Each needs a condition: the REST plugin (2017), alwaysSelectFullNamespace (2018), or forced OGNL evaluation of user input in tag attributes (2020).

incidents.name: Earlier OGNL remote code execution flaws (S2-008, S2-016, S2-032, S2-048)
incidents.note: Four older code execution flaws, all in CISA KEV. CVE-2013-2251 (action:, redirect: prefixes) and CVE-2012-0391 need nothing special; CVE-2016-3081 needs Dynamic Method Invocation on; CVE-2017-9791 needs the Struts 1 plugin and has no single fixed release in its record, so every 2.1.x and 2.3.x is flagged.

incidents.name: mod_rewrite filesystem mapping (code execution or source disclosure)
incidents.note: Needs mod_rewrite rules whose substitution starts with a backreference or variable. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: mod_proxy request forgery and local root escalation
incidents.note: Both in CISA KEV. CVE-2021-40438 lets a crafted request make mod_proxy forward to a server the attacker picks (used in ransomware attacks per KEV); it needs mod_proxy on. CVE-2019-0211 is local: code already running in a child process, such as a hosted script, becomes root at the next graceful restart.

incidents.name: Axis 1.x SOAP fault class instantiation RCE
incidents.note: Unauthenticated remote class instantiation through a crafted SOAP fault. Axis 1.x is end of life with no upstream fix; CISA added it to KEV on 18 November 2026. Rapid7 saw it exploited against Confluence Data Center (with the SOAP remote API on) and N-able N-central (with the Legacy API on) from 13 November; a Metasploit module followed on 17 November.

incidents.name: inflate() gzip header extra-field overflow
incidents.note: Only applications that call inflateGetHeader are affected. It set off advisories from most vendors that bundle zlib; proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: Expat 2.4.5 parser memory corruption
incidents.note: Reachable by parsing untrusted XML. Triggered advisories across vendors that bundle Expat.

incidents.name: Variable-font subglyph out-of-bounds write
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV since May 2025. Triggered by parsing a crafted font.

incidents.name: PNG sbit heap overflow (Chrome zero-day)
incidents.note: Heap overflow when loading embedded PNG bitmaps in a font. Exploited through Chrome in October 2020 and in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: Server authentication bypass
incidents.note: Only products that use libssh as an SSH server are exposed; clients are not. Public exploits exist.

incidents.name: Daemon checksum-length heap overflow
incidents.note: Reachable by anyone who can connect to an rsync daemon with anonymous read access. One of six rsync bugs disclosed together in January 2025; fixed in 3.4.0.

incidents.name: SambaCry
incidents.note: Needs a share the attacker can write to. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: DNSpooq
incidents.note: The two memory-corruption bugs of the DNSpooq set; both need DNSSEC validation turned on. Proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: VP8 encoder heap overflow
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild through browsers; in CISA KEV. Bundled the same way as libwebp.

incidents.name: Constructor deserialization RCE
incidents.note: Exploitable when the product parses untrusted YAML with the default Constructor. Public exploits exist, and it triggered advisories across Java vendors.

incidents.name: Polymorphic deserialization RCE
incidents.note: The first and one of the last of the 2017-2020 gadget-chain bugs. Exploitable only when the product turns on polymorphic (default) typing for untrusted JSON; public exploits exist.

incidents.name: InvokerTransformer deserialization gadget
incidents.note: The gadget chain behind the 2015 wave of Java deserialization attacks (WebLogic, WebSphere, JBoss, Jenkins). Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects; ysoserial has a ready-made payload.

incidents.name: Unmarshalling RCE
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild (VMware NSX Manager and Cloud Foundation); in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: Console JNDI remote code execution
incidents.note: Unauthenticated when the H2 web console is reachable; same JNDI root cause as Log4Shell. Public exploits exist.

incidents.name: Variable interpolation RCE
incidents.note: The same script, dns and url lookups as Text4Shell, reachable when untrusted values are interpolated. Commons Configuration 1.x is not affected.

incidents.name: Simple-query-mode SQL injection
incidents.note: Only with the non-default PreferQueryMode=SIMPLE. Rated 10.0 and patched in six branches at once, which set off advisories across Java vendors.

incidents.name: XFA-in-PDF XML external entity injection
incidents.note: Rated 10.0. Triggered by parsing a crafted PDF; the fix is in tika-core, so updating only the PDF parser module is not enough.

incidents.name: DiskFileItem deserialization RCE
incidents.note: Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects; a ysoserial payload exists.

incidents.name: snmptrapd buffer overflow
incidents.note: Only products that run snmptrapd and accept traps from untrusted hosts are exposed. Rated 9.8; proof-of-concept code is public. Distribution packages carry backported fixes.

incidents.name: Class-loader access through the class property
incidents.note: The bug behind the 2014 Struts 1 class-loader attacks (a Metasploit module exists). 1.9.4 was the first release to block the class property by default.

incidents.name: declaredClass property access on enums
incidents.note: Exploitable where property paths come from untrusted input. Triggered advisories across Java vendors in 2025.

incidents.name: MethodClosure deserialization gadget
incidents.note: Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects with Groovy on the classpath; ysoserial has a payload.

incidents.name: RegexRequestMatcher authorization bypass
incidents.note: Only applications that use RegexRequestMatcher with a dot in the pattern. Rated 9.8; proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: Pipe-device and format-string sandbox escapes
incidents.note: Code execution from a crafted PostScript, EPS or PDF file, which matters where the product converts or prints untrusted documents. Public exploits exist for both.

incidents.name: -dSAFER bypass through .rsdparams
incidents.note: Command execution from a crafted EPS file despite -dSAFER. Exploited in April 2017 and in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: ImageTragick
incidents.note: Command injection from a crafted image where the product converts untrusted uploads. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: ImageTragick file deletion and request forgery
incidents.note: The other two ImageTragick flaws in CISA KEV. A crafted image deletes files (EPHEMERAL coder) or makes the server send HTTP or FTP requests. Same fixed releases as CVE-2016-3714.

incidents.name: BIG-IP TMM iRule and APM stack overflows (out-of-band notification)
incidents.note: Six stack overflows (CWE-121) in the data plane, each 9.8 on CVSS 3.1: a request with no login can crash TMM and may run code. Each needs a specific setup on a virtual server: an iRule on client traffic using GENERICMESSAGE::route (CVE-2026-116953), DNS::scrape (CVE-2026-120722) or PEM::subscriber (CVE-2026-121805); an HTTP profile with an iRule using PSC::ip_address (CVE-2026-120285) or MR::message route (CVE-2026-120292); or an APM per-request policy with both the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents (CVE-2026-123637). So the check is your iRules and APM policies, not only the version. Affected: BIG-IP 21.1.0, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, and BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes and CNF 2.2.0 to 2.4.2; older branches are past support and were not evaluated. Fixes are engineering hotfixes only, with no workaround. The management side is not exposed. No exploitation has been reported, I found no public proof of concept, and none is in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-20. The same notification has four TMM crash-only flaws in APM (CVE-2026-125272, CVE-2026-126822, CVE-2026-126336, CVE-2026-121812), not tracked here.

incidents.name: BIG-IP APM OAuth heap overflow
incidents.note: Heap overflow (CWE-122, 9.8) that runs code with no login when BIG-IP APM acts as an OAuth Authorization Server on a virtual server; APM used only as an OAuth client or resource server is not exposed. F5 says it has been exploited and publishes indicators of compromise; in CISA KEV since 2026-09-22. A public exploit exists (watchTowr) that runs its payload inside TMM. Fixed in 21.1.0.3, 17.5.1.10 and 17.1.3.6. BIG-IP APM only; other modules and BIG-IP Next are not vulnerable. An earlier exploited APM flaw, CVE-2025-53521, is in the apmd process, not TMM, and is not tracked here.

incidents.name: NetScaler 2026 exploited flaws
incidents.note: Six flaws from five 2026 bulletins, all in CISA KEV. The worst are CVE-2026-88771 (code execution with no login in the default configuration, 9.5) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow through DTLS, on by default on a VPN virtual server); Citrix says both have been exploited on unmitigated systems. CVE-2026-19490 is an authentication bypass and CVE-2026-8452 and CVE-2026-88779 are memory overflows on appliances set up as a Gateway or AAA virtual server; CVE-2026-3055 is a memory over-read when set up as a SAML identity provider. Being current on 14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28 (FIPS: 14.1-73.41 FIPS, 13.1-37.282) covers all six. Citrix-managed cloud services are patched by Citrix.

components.name: Fortinet FortiOS (shared code in FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager and others)

incidents.name: FortiCloud SSO login bypass
incidents.note: Two ways around the FortiCloud single sign-on admin login, both in CISA KEV. With CVE-2025-59718 a forged SAML message logs in with no account (9.1); with CVE-2026-24858 anyone with a FortiCloud account and a registered device could log in to other customers' devices (9.4). Fortinet found the second being exploited by two FortiCloud accounts in January 2026. Only devices with FortiCloud SSO login on are exposed: it is off from the factory but is switched on when a device is registered to FortiCare from the GUI unless the admin unticks it. Turning it off is the interim fix (set admin-forticloud-sso-login disable).

incidents.name: CAPWAP daemon heap overflow
incidents.note: Heap overflow in the cw_acd daemon of FortiOS and FortiSwitchManager: a crafted request with no login can run code. Fortinet rates it hard to exploit because of ASLR and PIE (7.4), but it is in CISA KEV since 2026-09-09.

incidents.name: PAN-OS 2026 exploited flaws
incidents.note: Three flaws in different services, all in CISA KEV, with exploitation or exploit attempts reported by Palo Alto Networks for each. CVE-2026-0300: buffer overflow in the User-ID Authentication Portal (captive portal), code execution as root with no login on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have the portal on. CVE-2026-0257: GlobalProtect portal and gateway authentication bypass where authentication override cookies are on; also reaches Prisma Access; used in ransomware attacks per KEV. CVE-2026-0322: code execution in the management interface for a logged-in user, firewalls and Panorama. Keeping the captive portal and the management interface off untrusted networks removes most of the risk for the first and third.

components.name: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA (also inside FTD)

incidents.name: ASA and FTD remote access VPN exploited flaws
incidents.note: Four flaws in the SSL remote access VPN web service shared by ASA and FTD, all in CISA KEV. CVE-2025-20333 (code execution as root for a VPN user, 9.9) and CVE-2025-20362 (reaching restricted URLs with no login) are chained; Cisco reported a new attack variant in November 2025 that reloads unpatched devices. CVE-2026-20349 and CVE-2026-76418 let a request with no login reload the device (8.6 each). Only devices with the SSL VPN or other SSL listen sockets enabled are exposed; fixed releases differ by train, so use the Cisco Software Checker. Firewall Management Center is not affected by any of the four.

incidents.note: Every CVE here is one CISA lists as exploited in this product family. Listed from the KEV catalog (2014 to 2024) so they can be found by CVE; no vendor statements have been read for them yet.

incidents.name: IOS XE web UI takeover
incidents.note: Chained in mass compromises in October 2023: CVE-2023-20198 (10.0) creates an administrator with no login through the web UI, and CVE-2023-20273 uses that account to run commands as root and plant an implant. Both in CISA KEV. Only IOS XE devices with the HTTP or HTTPS server feature on are exposed; ip http active-session-modules none (and the secure- equivalent) blocks it.

incidents.name: SNMP stack overflow
incidents.note: Stack overflow in the SNMP subsystem of IOS and IOS XE. A crafted SNMP packet from a low-privileged user reloads the device; with high privileges it runs code as root (7.7). It needs valid SNMP credentials or a community string, and every SNMP version is affected. In CISA KEV since 2025-09-29. No workaround; excluding the affected OID is the mitigation.

incidents.name: Earlier exploited flaws (CISA KEV)
incidents.note: Every CVE here is one CISA lists as exploited in this product family. Listed from the KEV catalog (2004 to 2023) so they can be found by CVE; no vendor statements have been read for them yet.

incidents.name: SD-WAN peering authentication bypass
incidents.note: Two flaws in peering authentication (10.0 each): a crafted request with no login gets an internal high-privileged account on the Controller, then NETCONF access to change the SD-WAN fabric's configuration. CVE-2026-20182 was found after the first fix. Controller, Manager and Validator are affected whatever their configuration; internet-exposed control components are the ones at risk. Both in CISA KEV. No workaround. Cisco publishes indicators of compromise and asks suspected victims to open a TAC case.

incidents.name: Earlier exploited flaws (CISA KEV)
incidents.note: These are in the SD-WAN Manager (and one in the older SD-WAN software); CISA lists each as exploited. Listed from the KEV catalog (2022 to 2026) so they can be found by CVE; no vendor statements have been read for them yet.

components.name: Cisco AsyncOS (Secure Email Gateway, Secure Email and Web Manager)

incidents.name: Spam Quarantine remote command execution
incidents.note: A request with no login runs commands as root through the Spam Quarantine feature (10.0). Cisco found it in December 2025 during an attack campaign that left a persistence mechanism on appliances; Talos tracks the actor as UAT-9686. Only appliances with Spam Quarantine on and reachable from the internet are exposed, and the feature is off by default. In CISA KEV. No workaround.

incidents.name: Earlier exploited flaws (CISA KEV)
incidents.note: CISA lists both as exploited in Secure Email Gateway. Listed from the KEV catalog (2026 to 2026) so they can be found by CVE; no vendor statements have been read for them yet.

incidents.name: vCenter 2026 exploited flaws
incidents.note: Three flaws reachable by anyone with network access to vCenter, each 9.8 and in CISA KEV. CVE-2026-123890: authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service (VMSA-2026-0009), used as a zero-day since early September 2026 according to Mandiant; in KEV since 2026-11-20, a day after publication. CVE-2026-59310: directory traversal in the Syslog server leading to code execution (VMSA-2026-0006); KEV flags it as used in ransomware attacks. CVE-2024-37079: DCERPC heap overflow (VMSA-2024-0012); Broadcom said in January 2026 it has information that it was exploited. No workarounds. vCenter 7.0 only gets fixes under an extended support contract.

incidents.name: Property binder remote code execution
